title: Beyond the 956: Former Louisiana officer sentenced to three life terms and chemical castration in child rape case
excerpt: Former New Roads police officer and volunteer firefighter Kedreyon K. Williams, 31, was sentenced to three life terms without parole Thursday after a jury convicted him of raping three boys, ages 8 to 11. A Louisiana judge also ordered chemical castration.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A former New Roads, Louisiana, police officer and volunteer firefighter was sentenced to three life terms in prison without the possibility of parole Thursday, November 12, 2026, after a jury convicted him of raping three boys, ages 8 to 11.

Kedreyon K. Williams, 31, was also ordered to undergo chemical castration, an additional punishment sought by District Attorney Tony Clayton and granted by District Judge Kevin Kimball in Pointe Coupee Parish. The district attorney's office clarified that the castration will be chemical, not surgical.

A 12-member jury deliberated for just 39 minutes before finding Williams guilty on October 1, 2026, of three counts of first-degree rape of juveniles, indecent behavior with a juvenile, and possession of pornography involving juveniles. Each first-degree rape conviction carries a mandatory life sentence.

Prosecutors said the abuse took place at fire stations where Williams volunteered, at a business where he worked, and at his home. Williams was also convicted of having a video on his phone showing a child performing a sex act on him. He served as a part-time officer with the New Roads Police Department from October 2017 to May 2019, and was arrested in July 2024 by the Pointe Coupee Parish Sheriff's Office.

Judge Kimball described the case as the worst case of child sexual abuse he had ever encountered. The victims have not been named.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) on Instagram; Louisiana First News.
